dek: A Las Vegas professional bettor known as Krackman, seen on Showtime's Action, VSiN and FOX Sports Radio. He sells picks on WagerTalk from $39 a day to $1,999 a year, and his app, first sold as KrackWins, now runs as The Hot Picks at $99 to $499 a month. The guarantee pays store credit, every record we saw is kept or chosen by the seller, and buyer posts are few and split.

short_answer: Bill Krackomberger is a real and well known professional bettor based in Las Vegas. Press coverage going back to 2014 describes him as a full time bettor who moved from North Jersey, and he starred in Showtime's 2019 series Action. Today he hosts on FOX Sports Radio and VSiN, sells picks on WagerTalk, and is the face of a subscription app published by Krack Enterprises LLC. In that narrow sense he is a legitimate seller.

The app has changed. It launched in 2019 as KrackWins and its website promised that it was the only place to find his bets. The krackwins.com address no longer loaded on 20 Nov 2026, and the same Google Play app now appears as TheHotPicks, sold by The Hot Picks LLC as picks from "a team of Vegas legends" with no Krackman branding we could see. We could not confirm who makes the app's picks today.

Whether his paid picks make money for buyers is not shown anywhere independent. WagerTalk shows strong runs, such as 109-73 for +50.4 units in the NFL since 14 Dec, but each starts on a date the seller picked. The Last 20 table on 20 Nov 2026 was 10 and 10, a small loss at the listed odds. In 2019 he told The Ringer that a pro is happy to get back 101 or 102 for every 100 wagered, which is a useful yardstick for any bigger claim.

Buyer posts are few and split: warm App Store reviews, three critical or mixed Google Play reviews from 2019 and 2021, and one forum buyer in Feb 2026 who said his baseball picks were not worth the money. If you buy, buy short, treat the guarantee as store credit, and record every pick with the price you got.

guarantee: On WagerTalk the guarantee applies to guaranteed daily picks only. The site says that if "your daily pick(s) package does not result in an overall profit across all included plays," the paid cash value is credited back to your account for use on a later daily package, daily guaranteed package or multiple day package. That is store credit, not cash, and it does not apply to season or yearly passes.

The WagerTalk refund policy says "All Sales are Final and products are sold 'as is'" and that once a product is purchased, delivered or viewed, no refunds will be issued. It also lists cases where refunds will not be issued because of regulatory limits, such as in state college teams.

The app has no performance guarantee that we could find. The store listings say subscriptions renew automatically unless turned off at least 24 hours before the period ends, that the current period cannot be cancelled once started, and that any unused free trial time is forfeited when you buy. The Hot Picks pricing page says the average number of plays is "representative" and not a guaranteed amount.
Nothing covers losses on the bets themselves, which for most buyers will be far larger than the package price.

claims_note: How we checked: we took each record shown on his WagerTalk profile on 20 Nov 2026, worked out the win rate, and compared the unit total with what the same record would make at flat stakes and standard -110 odds. Where the posted units are about double the flat figure, the result depends on how much was staked on each rated play, which the streak does not show.

Each Hot Streak starts on a date the seller or store picked, such as 14 Dec for the NFL or 6 Dec 2025 for the 5% plays. A run cut from a longer history tells you little; every handicapper has a hot stretch somewhere. The Last 20 table is the only unfiltered slice on the page, and on 20 Nov 2026 it was even.

His own words are the best yardstick. In 2019 he told The Ringer he works on very small margins and is happy to get back 101 or 102 for every 100 wagered. A buyer who pays for picks and bets them at slightly worse prices can easily lose a margin that thin.

In 2020 he publicly accused William Hill of delaying in game bets, which the book called "absolutely outrageous." That, and his bans at some books, show he is an active bettor; it does not show how his paid picks perform.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing complete that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every pick he sold with the line and odds, kept by an outside party, and no court or regulator action about his pick service in what we could open.

What WagerTalk shows: a Last 20 table, Hot Streaks and a Who's Hot board, all graded by the store that sells his picks. On 20 Nov 2026 the Last 20 was 10 and 10, mostly college basketball sides and NFL player props. The Who's Hot board listed him at 23-20-0 for $1,629 over the last 7 days in one table and 12-3-0 for $2,883 in another sport tab. On 16 Nov 2026 the same Last 20 table had shown 16 wins, 3 losses and 1 no play, which shows how fast a 20 play window swings.

Forum users quoted different numbers: a TheRX post in Dec 2025 put his 2025 college football record at 70-56, while WagerTalk shows 91-69-2 for the 2025/26 college football season. The windows may differ, but neither is an audited log.

Background: BuzzFeed's 2014 profile described him as a solo bettor who had moved from North Jersey to Las Vegas seven years earlier, spread his action over many $300 to $500 bets, and gave occasional tips for free rather than selling picks. The KrackWins app launched in 2019, around the time of the Showtime series; its Google Play listing names Krack Enterprises LLC at a Las Vegas suite address as developer, shows Right Side Sports LLC as the seller, and links to website terms from The Hot Picks LLC.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Bill Krackomberger pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Bill Krackomberger performs.
our_data.context: For scale: the streaks on his WagerTalk profile run from about 57% to 60% winners, and his Last 20 on 20 Nov 2026 was 50%. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence on Bill Krackomberger is thin. Most of it is app store reviews and forum users sharing his plays. Below is everything we found, positive and negative, and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found about ten buyer comments from 2019 to 2026 across the App Store, Google Play and TheRX. The App Store reviews shown are warm: users praise real time alerts, the discipline and bankroll lessons, and one says he won about 60% of plays. Google Play is cooler: in 2019, the year the app launched, one buyer called it a cash grab riding the Showtime series and complained about missing unit ratings and higher prices, and another said a promised month of free picks lasted two weeks; the developer answered both and offered fixes. A 2021 premium buyer ended a month in profit but said the weekly recap did not match the plays he received. On TheRX in Dec 2025 and Feb 2026 users mostly passed his plays around and floated a group buy of a year, and one buyer said his baseball picks were not worth the money. We found no Sportsbook Review or Covers thread about his service, no BBB listing for Krack Enterprises, and no post about him in our Reddit library. The pattern is a known bettor with a small, split buyer file, not a run of billing complaints.
An App Store reviewer defended the app and its host, said losing stretches are normal, and put bad experiences down to unrealistic expectations or not following the guidance.

Another App Store reviewer, a longtime radio listener, said he moved from the free tier to higher plans over about two years, had some big wins and some losing streaks, and was ahead overall. He called the app "a lesson in discipline."
An App Store reviewer who upgraded from the free trial to the Standard plan said he got picks several times a week and had won at about a 60% rate so far. The developer thanked him in Jan 2023.

The App Store shows a 3.8 out of 5 average from 62 ratings, and Google Play shows 3.6 from 93 reviews with more than 10,000 downloads. Only a few written reviews are visible on either store, so the lower ratings behind those averages are mostly unseen. The old krackwins.com home page also carried hand picked praise from users.

A Google Play reviewer said the picks were useless without a unit rating, that alerts vanished when opened, and that prices went up while the product shrank after people had subscribed, calling the app a cash grab on the Showtime hype. The developer replied that unit guides came with the higher plans, that the basic plan had been a $29 launch promotion with a regular price of $49, and offered a free month.

Another Google Play reviewer said he changed his rating from 5 stars to 1 because he got two weeks of free picks instead of the promised month, and the bonus picks he was sent had no dates. The developer said it had emailed him, extended his free picks and added bonus picks.

A Google Play reviewer who joined the premium plan for a month said he started with a great week, leveled off and finished the month in profit, but felt he did not get all the picks, because the weekly recap and record did not match the plays sent to him.
On TheRX, a user shared two of his bowl plays and listed his 2025 college football record as 70-56. Another user said he planned to buy a 5% play and report back; we did not see a follow up result.
A TheRX user asked whether anyone had his Super Bowl 5% play and props and floated a group buy of a full year for $1,188. Later in the thread another user posted the Super Bowl plays.

In the same thread, a user who said he bought the service for baseball wrote that he quit after about a month, tried again after the All Star break with no improvement, and judged it not worth the money.

A BBB search for Krack Enterprises returned no business listing, so there is no BBB complaint history to read. Our Reddit library and web searches found no Reddit, Sportsbook Review or Covers thread reviewing his paid picks.

conflicts: WagerTalk sells his picks and keeps the record, the Hot Streaks and the Who's Hot board that promote them. The store has a direct interest in how he looks.
The guarantee is sold by the same store and pays in store credit, which keeps a losing buyer spending there.
His radio work is sponsored by sportsbooks; the FOX Sports Radio show he hosts is presented by BetMGM. That does not change his record, but it is a business tie worth knowing.
The app that carried his name now sells picks under The Hot Picks brand from an unnamed team. A buyer who signs up because of his name may not be getting his plays.
strengths: A real, publicly known bettor with years of independent press coverage, from BuzzFeed in 2014 to The Ringer in 2019.
WagerTalk shows his last 20 plays with the line, odds and result, including losing days, and prices every package.
Short, cheap ways to test him: a day for $39 or a three day pass on sale for $49.
In interviews he is candid that pros work on thin margins of 1% to 2%, which sets honest expectations.
The developer answered critical app reviews publicly and offered fixes and free time.
concerns: No full, independent record. Every streak starts on a date the seller or store chose, and the posted unit totals are about double what the same records make at flat stakes.
The paid guarantee returns credit, not cash, and WagerTalk says all sales are final.
The app was rebranded from KrackWins to The Hot Picks, and we could not confirm who makes its picks now.
App plans run up to $499 a month, trials turn into paid plans automatically, and the pricing page gives two different trial terms.
Few independent buyer posts. Of the detailed ones outside the curated app store reviews, most were negative or mixed, including a 2021 buyer who said the recap did not match the plays he received.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. Player prop unders at -115 need more than 53% to break even, and a 1% to 2% edge disappears if you get a worse number.
Before buying the app, ask who makes the picks today and whether they are the same plays sold on WagerTalk.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. WagerTalk's guarantee is account credit.
Cancel app trials before they renew if you only want to test the picks, and screenshot the trial terms you were shown.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get, and compare your tally with any weekly recap.
faq: He is a real, well known professional bettor in Las Vegas who sells picks on WagerTalk and fronted the KrackWins app, now branded The Hot Picks. Prices are published. We could not verify that his paid picks win over time, because the records we saw are kept or chosen by the seller, and we found no court or regulator action involving his pick service.
How much does Bill Krackomberger cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 WagerTalk sold passes from $39 for a day to $1,999 for a year, with a year on sale for $1,188 and three day sport passes at $49. Season packages ran from $259 to $719. App plans were $99.99 to $499.99 a month, plus a $159 weekly pass.
Does Bill Krackomberger have a verified record?

No. WagerTalk shows streaks such as 109-73 in the NFL since 14 Dec and a last 20 table, all kept by the store that sells his picks. On 20 Nov 2026 that last 20 was 10 and 10. We found no independent, time stamped log of every pick.
Is KrackWins the same as The Hot Picks?

The Google Play app with the package name com.krackwins.app now appears as TheHotPicks, from the same developer, Krack Enterprises LLC, and krackwins.com no longer loads. The Hot Picks site describes a team of professional bettors and did not name him in what we read, so ask the seller who makes the picks.
What do buyers say about Bill Krackomberger?

The few buyers we found are split. App Store reviews praise the discipline and real time alerts; Google Play reviews from 2019 and 2021 complain about missing unit sizes, shortened trials and a recap that did not match the plays sent; one forum buyer in 2026 said his baseball picks were not worth it.

You get the plays of a known professional bettor in real time. What is unproven is whether his paid picks beat break even over hundreds of plays at the prices buyers actually get, given that he describes pro margins as 1% to 2%. The guarantee pays store credit only, and nothing refunds your betting losses.
